audit_result.proof_trace: The `delete_authorization_code` RPC is only called on the expiry path (L101) and the success path (L151-152); on client-mismatch (L83-88), redirect-URI mismatch (L90-95), PKCE failure (L116-120), and user-not-found (L130-135) exit paths the code is fetched but never deleted, violating the single-use post-condition. Additionally, the fetch (`get_authorization_code`) and delete are separate non-atomic RPCs, opening a concurrent double-issuance window where two simultaneous requests both pass the fetch before either deletes.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker who obtains a valid authorization code and its corresponding code_verifier submits two concurrent POST requests; both pass `get_authorization_code` before either reaches the delete, and both receive a distinct access token from the same single-use code. Separately, on PKCE failure the code remains live in the DB, though S256 makes verifier brute-force computationally infeasible.

PROP-stem-system-post-001.text: After authorization code exchange, the code must be deleted from the database.
